thread:
maya: Heads up — saw a big spike in embed quota from the nightly bulk ingest tests. Console shows huge per-call token counts and our quota alarms fired. Anyone else?
chris: Yup saw it at ~02:10 UTC. Alerts page shows 10x normal token/batch for the embed route.
linh: Did we change batching heuristics? I remember a PR changed the default behavior for the client libs.
maya: That's my suspicion. We rolled py/ts SDK 1.4.0 to canary yesterday. It added "auto_bulk=true" to the high-level embeddings API.
alex: @linh do we have the PR link?
linh: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/402 (note: internal link) — default changed to attempt larger batch windows for throughput.
chris: Example python call that now explodes token usage:
```python
# before (1.3.x)
client.embeddings.create(model="embed-32k", input=batch_of_texts, batch_size=64)
# after (1.4.0) - auto_bulk kicks in and coalesces into very large requests
client.embeddings.create(model="embed-32k", input=batch_of_texts)  # defaults to auto_bulk=True
```
maya: Console attribution is also confusing — the per-route tile aggregates by route_name but the bulking means one upper-level request attributed to the api/org not individual customer routes. We lost per-tenant visibility.
ops-bot: deploy-bot: Canary rollout of sdk@1.4.0 completed to 12% of accounts at 2024-10-11T02:05:12Z.
alex: That telemetry gap is the UX issue. If the SDK coalesces multiple logical requests into one physical call we need preserved routing metadata or per-input breakdown in the request payload.
linh: We debated carrying per-item tags when serializing batches but it was left out for perf reasons. We can add a compact index: route_tags: [r1,r2,...] and an offsets array.
chris: Short term mitigation ideas: 1) revert default in SDK to auto_bulk=false, 2) server-side guard to cap tokens-per-request and split, 3) enhance console to show estimated logical batch size via heuristic.
maya: Ops prefers server-side defensive split to avoid hot customers getting throttled. But devex wants SDK revert because unexpected behavior broke quota dashboards for customers.
linh: Reverting default is a small patch (publish 1.4.1). I'll raise it now.
linh: Proposed change in PR: set auto_bulk default to false and expose opt-in flag via client config.
```diff
- DEFAULT_AUTO_BULK = True
+ DEFAULT_AUTO_BULK = False  # revert to safe default
```
alex: For the console: can we add a quick telemetry metric embed.logical_batch_count and embed.physical_tokens to help reconcile? We already have token counts but not logical_batch_count.
maya: +1. Add a sampling path for per-item attribution for the next two weeks while we roll back. Maybe sample 5% of bulk requests and log full per-item metadata to the telemetry pipeline (s3/raw).
chris: Also add a soft quota alarm for tokens-per-physical-request so ops can throttle before org-level quota burns through.
linh: I'll queue 3 tasks: 1) SDK revert PR (1.4.1), 2) server-side hard-split guard (platform runtime), 3) telemetry sampling + console tile to show logical_batch estimates.
maya: Timeline?
linh: SDK patch in 2-3 hours; server-side guard needs a bit more testing — target EOD. Telemetry + console tile is a 2-sprint job but sampling can ship in 3 days.
alex: For the rollout UX: we should update the release notes and console banner for affected customers. Also add a diagnostic endpoint to map physical request -> original SDK version and sample id.
maya: Agreed. Also ping support to prepare canned responses for any customers seeing quota surprises. @chris can you draft the support blurb? :thumbsup:
chris: Will do — short note + links to how to opt-out of auto_bulk and how we plan to fix console attribution.
ops-bot: incident-bot: Created incident INC-2024-embed-bulk-quota and assigned to eng-platform.
maya: Thanks all. Keep thread updated when SDK patch is published and when the guard goes live.
linh: Patch merged to main, publishing 1.4.1 now. I'll post the published tag and canary coords in a follow-up. :rocket:
